Episodes 1 to 10 of 18 are authored: 770 entities, 4,022 exact mentions in original-en and 4,095 in modern-en, 768 of the 770 bound in the older edition and 765 in the modern one, 98 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-15.10. NEXT: episode 11 (Sirens, 635 paragraphs), the Ormond bar. 3,794 paragraphs remain; the long ones are 15 (Circe, 1,441), 17 (Ithaca, 654) and 12 (566); episode 18 (Penelope) is eight paragraphs of monologue and will be the densest in the book.

THE RULE THAT GOVERNS THIS BOOK: A SURNAME IS ALMOST NEVER ONE MAN, SO KEY BY DEFAULT AND ALIAS ONLY ON PROOF. AND THE COROLLARY, LEARNED THE HARD WAY IN EPISODES 8, 9 AND 10: RUN THE WHOLE-BOOK OCCURRENCE LIST ON EVERY ALIAS, NOT ONLY ON EVERY KEY. Three aliases have now been caught reaching past the episode that justified them -- PIPER into Peter Piper's tongue-twister at 9:117 (suppressed), LUCY into S. Lucy at 12:513 (keyed), and JOHN MULLIGAN into 'Malachi Roland St John Mulligan' at 14:47 (keyed). Each was found by a test, not by the build.

THE SURNAME DEDALUS NOW HAS THREE OWNERS: episodes 1-2 STEPHEN, episodes 6-8 his father SIMON, episode 9 the son again (9:136, 9:181, 9:224, 9:355), and episode 10 all three at once plus THE FOUR SISTERS -- Katey, Boody, Maggy and Dilly. At 10:71 and 10:84 the surname covers two girls at once and is deliberately left unbound; each girl is bound on her own first name. A test pins every exception.

THREE PEOPLE GOT THEIR NAMES IN EPISODE 10 AND THEIR EPISODE-8 CARDS WERE REWRITTEN RATHER THAN DUPLICATED: the Dedalus daughter outside Dillon's auctionrooms is DILLY; the soldier Myler Keogh beat is SERGEANTMAJOR BENNETT; the lord lieutenant of the Mirus bazaar placard is WILLIAM HUMBLE, EARL OF DUDLEY. When a later episode names somebody an earlier one only described, EXTEND THE EXISTING CARD -- never author a second one.

A GUARD TRAP WORTH REMEMBERING: the alias guard is (?<![A-Za-z])...(?![A-Za-z]) for keyed tables but (?<!\w)...(?!\w) for aliases, and AN APOSTROPHE AND A HYPHEN ARE NOT WORD CHARACTERS. Also CASE MATTERS in both: Joyce writes 'lady Dudley', 'lord Edward Fitzgerald', 'major Sirr', 'sister Monica', 'silken Thomas' and 'saint Patrick' with lowercase initials where the modern edition capitalises them, and the modern edition sets ELIJAH IS COMING in capitals at 10:115 and 10:351. Every one of those needed a second alias or a case-insensitive phrase.

THE MODERN EDITION IS A REWRITE AND CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It DELETES names (Chrysostomos 1:9, Mercury 1:293, Loyola 1:101, Adam Findlater and Dan Tallon 4:37, Hanlon 4:13, Wren 6:204, the Joe Miller 7:293, mother Dana 9:157, Aubrey 9:294, Barabbas 10:444) and SUPPLIES names Joyce did not write (Aristotle 3:0, Brian Boru 3:57, Deasy 3:10, Queen Victoria 3:94, M'Coy 5:27, Daniel O'Connell 6:106/6:277/6:278, Madame Bloom 6:104, Shakespeare 6:333, Martha 6:386, Nannetti 7:42/7:62, Bloom 7:67, Patrick Dignam 7:99, Gallaher 7:358, Mario 7:27, Long John Fanning 7:45, Boylan 8:35/8:255, Lot's wife 8:35, Charles Stewart Parnell 8:141, Reuben J. Dodd 8:12/8:364, the blind man 8:360, Ben Jonson 9:18, Madame Blavatsky 9:25, Queen Elizabeth 9:256, Saint Patrick 9:207/9:235, Mrs Shakespeare 9:255, Magee the Elder 9:315, Lady Gregory 9:450, Shakespeare 9:184/9:309/9:340/9:423, Oscar Wilde 10:526). IT ALSO SPLITS JOYCE'S COMPOUNDS, WHICH MAKES A NAME BINDABLE THAT WAS NOT: 'Jesusmario' (7:27) becomes 'Jesus-Mario', 'pseudomalachi' (9:194) 'false Malachi', 'Sonmulligan' (9:331) 'Son-Mulligan', 'Rutlandbaconsouthamptonshakespeare' (9:328) 'Rutland-Bacon-Southampton-Shakespeare' and 'Besteglinton' (9:286) 'Best-Eglinton'. Five entities are reachable in one edition only: BRIAN BORU and LOT'S WIFE in the modern alone, ADAM FINDLATER, MOTHER DANA and JOHN AUBREY in the older alone.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. Four cases, all keyed now: '_Los Demiurgos_' 3:1, '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' 4:162, '_That's not Mulcahy_' 6:325, '_Mr MacTrigger_' 8:208 and 8:223. The MacTrigger case was found by the omittedEntities line in the validation report and by nothing else -- READ THAT LINE ON EVERY BUILD. Over all 18 episodes the italic check also reports STEPHEN at 15:1133 (a stage direction, will need a key when Circe is read) and PATRICE at 16:212 (which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice' and will need suppressing); the two remaining hits, at 9:167 and 9:333, are play titles and are correct as they stand.

A SECOND SILENT FAILURE, FOUND IN EPISODE 8 AND NOW GUARDED: A REPEATED DICT LITERAL IN SPLIT OR PHRASE SHADOWS THE EARLIER ONE AND EVERY KEY IN IT CEASES TO EXIST. Duplicate 'Jack' and 'Paddy Dignam' tables had been dropping the episode 6 and 7 keys with every test green, and nine more duplicates were created and merged while authoring episode 10. Tables.test_no_split_or_phrase_key_is_declared_twice parses the source and fails on any repeated key. NEVER RE-DECLARE A TABLE -- MERGE INTO THE EXISTING LITERAL.
